comments:
> server_port = 1700 

> Two tests running at the same time, and specifically running this test recipe simultaneously will obviously compete for resources.

True!

> We did resolve this very same issue, a few years ago, with the util/perl/TLSProxy code. Can we do it again?

Hmm, the TLSProxy code looks like a very heavyweight solution. 
Can anyone who was involved in it (apparently, mostly @mattcaswell) 
refactor it in a way such that it is usable also for tests like those in `80-test_cmp_http.t`?
#14966 likely relates to this.  With the AFL it seems to be highly repeatable.  I'm not sure it is actually fuzzing anything though.
The intermittent test failures have a different source than #14966 - see my comment there.

I didn't mean to say that we should use TLSProxy with the Mock server.  All I want is a mechanism for it to listen on a *random port* rather than a static one.

What TLSProxy does is to run `openssl s_server` with `-accept localhost:0`.  and then parses the output for the line saying `ACCEPT:`, which specifies the address and actual port.  The Mock server could be made to do something similar.
Good thought - i'm going to do something like that now.

review_comments: Please make an aux function out of that, rather than copying code from `s_socket.c`, and use it in both places.
BTW, nice trick to use `BIO_set_accept_port(acbio, port)` with `port` being 0 to auto-select any available local port. Please document this special feature in `doc/man3/BIO_s_accept.pod`.

That nice trick should be common knowledge...  I'm again surprised how many do not know of this.
I can recommend "UNIX Network Programming" by Richard W. Stevens

My knowledge of network programming is unfortunately very spotty.
Anyway, `BIO_set_accept_port()` is defined by OpenSSL, so its features should be documented there.
Also because this feature hopefully is usable also on non-UNIX systems ;-)
Done with the aux function.  Good idea
I'm proposing a respective doc extension in #15354.
